wheel.title: Wheel of Luck
wheel.subtitle: A wheel that spins on stream and hands out prizes to your viewers.

empty.title: You don't have a wheel yet
empty.body: Create one, fill it with the prizes you want to give away, and drop its link into OBS. Viewers earn spins by supporting your channel.
empty.modePrizesHelp: Viewers earn spins by supporting the channel and win whatever the segment holds.
empty.modeRaffleHelp: People sign up and the wheel picks a winner among them.

segments.title: Slices
segments.needTwo: A wheel needs at least 2 slices before it can spin.

prizes.templatePlaceholder: What the bot announces on a win
prizes.noSoundAlerts: You have no sound alerts set up

overlayUrl.title: Link for OBS
overlayUrl.help: Add it as a browser source in the scene where you want the wheel.

status.testSpun: The test spin landed on "{{label}}". Nothing was written to your history.
status.testFailed: Couldn't spin. Check that there are active slices with weight.

credits.title: How a spin is earned
credits.label: What your credits are called
credits.labelHelp: The name your viewers see in chat: tokens, points, tickets...
credits.priceHelp: How many credits each spin of this wheel uses up.
credits.accumulableHelp: With this on, small contributions add up until they reach the price. Off, each one has to be enough on its own.
credits.overflowHelp: When a contribution goes past the price but doesn't reach another spin.
credits.multiFit: If one contribution covers several spins
credits.multiFitHelp: A big cheer can pay for several spins. Decide how many here.
credits.expiryHelp: Pick end of stream and balances are cleared when you stop broadcasting.

sources.title: Where credits come from
sources.help: Turn on what you want to accept and set what it's worth. It reads: for every X, this many credits.
sources.rewardIdHelp: Only that reward counts. Without it, any redemption on your channel would add credits.
sources.tierHelp: Only here: it's the only source Twitch sends the tier through. Applied before the per-event cap.

triggers.title: How a spin is triggered
triggers.commandsHelp: Turn this off if you'd rather spin only from the panel.
triggers.autoSpinHelp: As soon as someone reaches the price the wheel spins without them typing anything. One spin per contribution, so animations don't stack up.
triggers.buyCommandHelp: Trades deca coins for credits. It only answers if you turned on the Deca coins source in the Credits tab.

limits.title: Anti-farming caps
limits.help: Brakes so a bad weight setup can't drain your economy in one afternoon.
limits.cooldownHelp: How long the same viewer must wait before spinning again. 0 = no wait.
limits.maxPerStreamHelp: Cap on how many spins one person can do in a stream. Empty = no cap.
limits.maxCoinsHelp: Ceiling on coins the wheel can hand out per hour. Past it, the prize goes to Deliveries. Empty = no ceiling.

rewards.title: Channel point rewards
rewards.help: Pick which redemptions give credits and how many. You can have several — a cheap one and a premium one, say.
rewards.empty: You're not listening to any redemption yet. Add one so viewers can earn credits with points.
rewards.loadFailed: We couldn't fetch your rewards from Twitch. Reconnect your account and reload.

test.title: Test it like it's live
test.help: Fire a contribution at this wheel without waiting for someone to donate.
test.notCredited: Nothing was credited. Usually that means the source is off, or the contribution didn't reach the price and the wheel doesn't keep what falls short.
test.notSpun: Didn't spin (spin on its own is off)
test.sourceOff: That source is off in the Credits tab, so the contribution won't credit anything.
test.warning: This isn't a rehearsal: it really credits, really spends and really spins on your overlay. Use a test name if you don't want to touch anyone's balance.

messages.title: What the bot says in your chat
messages.help: Every field comes with Decatron's wording. Type your own to replace it, or clear it to go back.
messages.unknownVars: These don't exist and will show up as-is in chat: {{vars}}

keys.winPending: When you hand the prize over yourself
keys.winMulti: When they spin several times at once
keys.choiceReady: When they bank spins and pick how many to spend
keys.bought: When they buy credits with deca coins
keys.notEnoughCoins: Tried to buy without enough coins
keys.buyTooSmall: Tried to buy less than one credit's worth
keys.buyNoAccount: Tried to buy without a Decatron account
keys.streamLimit: Out of spins for the stream

messages.editingIn: Editing the {{lang}} wording. The language is changed in Settings.

deliveries.title: Pending deliveries
deliveries.help: Prizes the bot couldn't deliver on its own. The reason comes from the bot: it tells you whether something needs fixing or you just have to hand it over.
deliveries.empty: Nothing pending. Everything that came up was delivered automatically.

raffle.needTwo: You need at least 2 entrants to draw.
raffle.entryCommandHelp: What viewers type in chat. Validated against the system's reserved commands.
raffle.windowModeHelp: Manual is opened and closed by you; timed closes itself; always open never closes.
raffle.windowSecondsHelp: How long the window stays open after you open it.
raffle.maxEntriesHelp: How many times one person can enter. Each ticket adds weight.
raffle.entryCostHelp: How many {{credits}} a ticket costs. 0 = free.
raffle.reqHelp: Who can enter. Adding someone manually from this panel skips these.
raffle.weightHelp: Each entry starts at 1 (or at its ticket count) and is multiplied by whatever you enable. Saving recalculates the whole pool.
raffle.wWatchtimeHelp: One multiplier point per X minutes watched, up to the cap.
raffle.wTierHelp: Decatron supporter tier, not the Twitch sub tier: chat doesn't send the tier.
raffle.wCoinsHelp: Uses the Decatron account's total spent, which is global and not per channel.
raffle.drawModeHelp: One winner; N winners in one round; or one and keep going.
raffle.winnersCountHelp: How many it picks each time you draw.
raffle.removeWinnerHelp: If off, the winner can come up again in the next draw.
raffle.clearOnEnd: Clear the pool when the stream ends
raffle.clearOnEndHelp: Applies when Twitch reports the stream went offline.
raffle.poolHelp: The percentage is each person's real probability with the current weights.

wheel.nameHelp: Just so you can tell them apart in the panel. The overlay URL doesn't change.
wheel.enabledHelp: Off it ignores commands and doesn't show in the overlay, and frees a slot in your plan.

quota.reached: You've hit your plan's limit of {{max}} wheel(s) on. Turn one off to create another.
quota.segmentsReached: Your plan allows {{max}} segments per wheel.

wheel.deleteConfirm: This deletes "{{name}}" along with its spin history and pending deliveries. It cannot be undone.

look.previewNeedsSegments: Add at least two segments in the Segments tab and your wheel shows up here.
look.colorsHelp: Changes show up instantly in the preview beside this.
look.accentHelp: Outer rim, needle and center dot.
look.inkHelp: Segment borders, center hub and the winner card background.
look.backgroundHelp: Transparent is what you want for OBS. Only pick a color if you use it outside a scene.
look.watermarkHelp: The discreet watermark in the corner of the overlay.
look.watermarkLocked: Can be hidden from the Premium plan up.
look.paletteHelp: Fallback colors, in order, for segments that did not pick their own.
look.centerHelp: Your logo or any image on the hub. With no image it draws a dot in the accent color.
look.centerPlaceholder: Pick from your library or paste a URL
look.turnsHelp: Full turns before stopping. A random extra one is added so two spins never look identical.
look.easingHelp: How it decelerates. Quint is the closest to a real wheel.
look.revealSecondsHelp: How long the winner stays on screen. With "Only while spinning", the wheel leaves the scene after this time.
look.visibilityHelp_spin: Hidden while idle. It comes in when a spin arrives and leaves after showing the winner; with queued spins it stays until the last one.
look.visibilityHelp_always: The wheel is on screen all the time, spinning or not.
look.celebrationHelp: What goes with the winner reveal.
look.soundsHelp: Touch nothing and Decatron's pack plays. You can mute any of them or use your own.
look.soundPlaceholder: Pick from your library or paste a URL
look.tickOnlyDefault: Decatron's or silence only: it plays dozens of times per spin and audio with a tail sounds awful repeated.
look.soundWhen_spin_tick: Every time the needle crosses a segment.
look.soundWhen_spin_slowdown: During the final stretch of the spin. It ends right as the wheel stops.
look.soundWhen_reveal: When it stops on the winning segment.
look.soundWhen_win_celebration: Along with the confetti, after the reveal.
look.soundWhen_raffle_draw: When the wheel starts drawing among the entrants.
look.soundWhen_raffle_winner: Along with the confetti, when the raffle winner comes out.
look.soundWhen_spin_tick_card: The drumroll while the card shakes, faster and faster until it flips.
look.typoHelp: The lettering on the segments and the winner card. The list is fixed on purpose: OBS doesn't have your computer's fonts installed, so a hand-typed font would look right here and come out as something else on stream.
look.fontHelp: Each option is shown in its own lettering.
look.fontWeightHelp: How heavy the segment lettering is.
look.fontOneWeight: This font ships with a single weight.
look.textScaleHelp: Scales every label at once. The wheel still shrinks them on its own for long labels and narrow segments, so they never spill out of the wedge.
look.textUppercaseHelp: Writes the labels in uppercase without retyping them.
look.textColorHelp: The text drawn on each segment.
look.textOutlineHelp: A border around the letters. Helps when the segments are light-coloured and the text gets lost.
look.presentationHelp: How the result gets drawn. The draw itself is the same in all of them: the server picks the winner and the presentation only animates up to it.
look.presentationRowHelp: Saved per wheel, not per channel: you can keep a big wheel for subs and a faster one for bits.
look.presentationOnlyOne: only the wheel for now; the strip, the reel and the grid plug in here
look.pointerHelpNeedle: The needle that marks the winning slice. Changing sides is not just cosmetic: the wheel stops offset so the needle keeps pointing at the right prize.
look.pointerHelpViewer: The frame around the winning cell. It is this presentation’s equivalent of the needle.
look.pointerHiddenHelp: The wheel still stops where it stops; the marker just is not drawn.
look.pointerSideHelp: Top is where everyone looks first, but you can move it if something in your scene covers that area.
look.pointerCapsHelp: The two tips are what make it read as a sight and not as a plain box.
look.pointerColorHelp: Follows the wheel accent color by default.
look.backgroundBoxNote: The background is painted around the wheel only, not across the whole screen. In the Canvas tab you can decide exactly which area it covers.
look.templatesHelp: A whole look in one click: colors, typography, pointer and celebration. They do not move anything around or change the draw format, and nothing is saved until you press Save.

media.title: Media library
media.help: Your usual library, filtered by the "wheel" category. Whatever you upload here can be picked in Look. Storage quota is your plan's, not a separate one for the wheel.

history.title: Spins
history.window: Your plan shows the last {{days}} days. History is never deleted: upgrade and it all comes back.
history.windowAll: Your plan shows the full history.
history.empty: No spins to show with these filters yet.
history.distTitle: What came up, and what should
history.distHelp: The thick bar is the real frequency; the thin one below it, the probability you configured. Metrics use the whole history, not just what the table shows.
history.fewSpins: With few spins the two bars will differ quite a bit, and that's normal: chance takes a while to look like its own table.

wallets.title: Contribution wallets
wallets.help: Each viewer's credit balance. They belong to the channel, not to one wheel: whoever contributes once can spend on any of your wheels.
wallets.empty: Nobody has credits on this channel yet.
wallets.lifetimeNote: The balance is set, not added to: type the number you want it to end at. Lifetime never goes down, not even when a balance is corrected by hand.

wheel.duplicated: Wheel duplicated. The copy is off: turn it on when it's ready.
wheel.duplicatedQuotaFull: Wheel duplicated, but your plan already has all its wheels on: turn one off to enable this one.
wheel.slugWarning: Changing it changes the overlay URL. If you already pasted it into OBS, you'll have to update it there.
wheel.slugChanged: Identifier changed. Remember to update the URL in OBS.
wheel.slugAdjusted: That identifier was taken; it ended up as “{{slug}}”. Update the URL in OBS.

rules.title: Draw rules
rules.help: They change which segment can come up. None of them touch the drawing: the wheel still shows every segment, whether it can come up or not.
rules.noRepeatHelp: Stops the same result coming up twice in a row. If the rule would leave a single possible segment, it's ignored: better a repeat than no spin.
rules.pityHelp: After several spins in a row with no prize, the next one can't be “nothing” again. Counted per viewer.
rules.multiHelp: Lets a viewer spend several spins at once. Each spin is its own draw: stock runs down between them.
rules.multiNote: In chat it's used like this: {{command}} 5. It's charged all at once or not at all, and the bot answers with a single summary message.

canvas.title: Overlay canvas
canvas.help: Place the wheel, the winner card and the watermark on a 1920x1080 screen. Drag to move, use the corners to resize.
canvas.autoNote: This wheel still centers itself and adapts to any browser source size in OBS. The moment you move something it switches to fixed 1920x1080 positions.
canvas.obsSize: This wheel has its own canvas: set the OBS browser source to {{width}}x{{height}} or the design will be off.
canvas.fixedNote: This wheel uses fixed 1920x1080 positions. The OBS browser source has to be exactly that size, or the design will be off.
canvas.bgColorNote: The color is chosen in the Look tab.
canvas.noImageYet: Pick an image or a video
canvas.videoNote: The video restarts every time the piece appears. In the panel it always plays muted.

liveTranslation.title: Live translation
liveTranslation.subtitle: Your voice is transcribed, translated and dubbed in real time. Each viewer picks their language from the Chrome extension; only they hear it.
liveTranslation.notConfigured: The server has no voice services configured; the feature can't start yet.
liveTranslation.confirmStop: Stop the current session? The app will stop sending audio until you press Start again.

live.hint: Open Decatron Desktop on your PC and press Start in “Live translation”. Listeners, phrases and credits show up here in real time.

app.title: 1 · Decatron Desktop on your PC
app.text: Captures your microphone and sends it to the server. Link it once from Settings → Integrations.

ext.title: 2 · Extension for your viewers
ext.text: Adds a 🌐 button to the Twitch player: they pick a language and hear the translation with captions.

config.title: Settings
config.subtitle: Which languages you offer and which voice each one uses.
config.targetsHint: A language is only translated while someone is listening; no listeners, no voice credits spent.
config.voicesHint: One voice per language. With the standard voice you pick among the installed Piper voices.
config.announceHint: The bot tells chat the stream can be heard in other languages. Use {languages} for the list.
config.announcePlaceholder: 🌐 This stream can be heard in {languages} with the Decatron Translate extension: https://decatron.net/translate
config.backgroundHint: Suggested volume of your voice while the translation plays. Each viewer can change it.
config.engineHint: The standard voice runs on our server and costs no credits; it takes a bit longer to start speaking. Premium voices sound better and respond sooner, but charge credits per character. If you run out of credits mid-stream, the voice falls back to standard on its own and nothing stops.

credits.title: Credits
credits.subtitle: One balance for everything that costs money: premium voice, live translation, LoL coach, !ia and AI chat. What runs on our server (standard voice) doesn't spend from here.
credits.purchasedHint: Never expire; used once the monthly ones run out.
credits.transition: Courtesy credits while you pick a plan, until {{date}}.
credits.expires: Your plan expires on {{date}}. Purchased credits are kept.
credits.empty: No credits: the coach, premium-voice translation, !ia and AI chat pause until you have balance. Standard voice keeps working.
credits.standardHint: Piper runs on our server and costs no money: it has its own generous quota, apart from credits.
credits.ratesHint: 1 million credits is about ${{usd}} of real cost for the platform. Each feature charges what it really costs.

rates.premiumVoiceSub: Per language: each extra language adds its voice.
rates.aiSub: Based on the model's real tokens; only if the call succeeded.

credits.orPlan: or get a monthly quota with a plan →

buy.title: Buy credits
buy.hint: Purchased credits never expire and are used once the monthly quota runs out. Pay by card or Yape (Culqi); charged in soles, you get your receipt or invoice.
buy.onlyOwner: Only the channel owner can buy credits.
buy.legal: Price in USD; charged in soles at the platform's fixed exchange rate. The electronic receipt arrives in a few minutes.
buy.success: Done! You received {{n}} credits. Your receipt arrives in a few minutes.

timerAdvanced.configureTimezoneFirst: Set your time zone in the General tab before creating a Happy Hour
timerAdvanced.confirmDeleteHappyHour: Are you sure you want to delete this Happy Hour?

timerAdvanced.errorManualActivate: Error starting the manual Happy Hour
timerAdvanced.errorManualDeactivate: Error stopping the manual Happy Hour
timerAdvanced.errorTogglingHappyHour: Error changing the Happy Hour status
timerAdvanced.happyHourDescription: Automatically multiplies the added time at specific times (e.g. x2 on weekends).
timerAdvanced.infoDescription: ℹ️ Advanced settings with preset templates, scheduled auto-pause and time multipliers.
timerAdvanced.name: Name
timerAdvanced.noCustomTemplates: You don't have custom templates yet
timerAdvanced.restoreDefaultsNote: Note: this will NOT delete your saved schedules or custom templates.
timerAdvanced.selectPartsToApply: Choose which parts of the template to apply
timerAdvanced.timezoneDescription: Sets the base time for the Auto-pause and Happy Hour features.
